/Issued 529 AM MDT Sat Oct 10 2026/ 

 - Meteorological Overview:

A complex evolution to the upper level pattern will ensue today, 
initially with a large upper level trough with multiple embedded 
vort maxes sinking southward from the Pacific Northwest, elongating 
as it does so. At the surface an area of low pressure centered in 
southern SK is propelling a cold front southward across the plains 
early this morning. The combination of this front, favorable 
forcing, and ample moisture will result in a round of precipitation 
developing through the day today. Initial precipitation type looks to 
be rain in many areas before cold air advection near the surface 
wins out and flips precipitation type to snow. Confidence is highest 
in snow developing early near the Southern Rocky Mountain Front, 
where a band of snow will aid in flipping precip type to snow by 
early afternoon. Snow characteristic looks to be the wet and heavy 
variety, especially at lower elevations, which raises concern for 
trees with leaves on them still seeing snapped branches, potentially 
impacting power lines. 

Colder air continues to sink southward into Southwest Montana 
heading into Sunday, though there remains some uncertainty with 
respect to just how far it makes it. Aloft the complex evolution 
continues, with the upper level troughing elongating further, while 
also interacting with the remnants of Rachel as they lift 
northeastward ahead of the trough axis. Ample moisture associated 
with not only the main troughing, but the remnants of Rachel will 
support the expansion of precipitation southward into Southwest 
Montana during the day Sunday as an upper level jet moves overhead.
The extent of impactful snowfall across Southwest Montana will 
follow where the coldest air both aloft and at the surface ends up
settling. Banded precipitation looks to persists into Monday 
morning across portions of Central and Southwest Montana before 
subsiding through the day. 

The region looks to dry out for at least a couple days as the upper 
level troughing consolidates once again across the desert Southwest. 
Uncertainty grows a bit toward Thursday, though the majority of 
ensemble members remain dry Thursday toward the weekend. -AM

 - Forecast Confidence & Scenarios:

Given marginal thermodynamics at times with respect to both the 
atmosphere and surface temperatures, it makes for quite the tricky 
snowfall/accumulation forecast. Overall there were no changes with 
this forecast cycle to ongoing winter highlights, but consideration 
was given to upgrades in a few areas:

 - Northern Rocky Mountain Front and adjacent plains: This area 
looks to have the most consistent thermodynamic environment 
supporting snow (Cold throughout), but the greatest forcing looks to 
remain further south. Given snowfall amounts vary quite a bit from 
north to south across these zones, the Winter Weather Advisory was 
left as is. Should amounts increase much in these zones, a Winter 
Storm Warning may become necessary. 

 - Helena Valley: The greatest uncertainty in the Helena area is 
with respect to just how quickly precipitation flips over to snow 
today/this evening. Either way, initial snow that falls will need to 
overcome warm pavement to begin accumulating, which looks 
questionable through late tonight given uncertainty with respect to 
snowfall rates. Colder air continues to make inroads Sunday which 
will allow for greater snowfall rates to result in more 
accumulations. Given marginal snowfall forecast totals, I elected to 
continue with the Winter Weather Advisory for now. 

 - Near and south of I-90 Sunday into Sunday night: Ample forcing 
and moisture moving in within a deep fetch of southwesterly flow 
aloft (Supported by Rachel's remnants) will foster some banded 
precipitation Sunday into Monday. The area of greatest concern would 
be along and south of a line from Dillon to Bozeman for the greatest 
precipitation amounts. This also happens to be the area of greatest 
uncertainty with respect to the colder air at the surface and aloft. 
Given there are Winter Weather Advisories in place already, and that 
there is still uncertainty with respect to temperatures, no upgrades 
to a Winter Storm Warning were made. This area will bear monitoring 
for any trends over the next 24 hours or so. -AM
